artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B_0,B_1,B_2,\dots$ denote the Bernoulli numbers, defined by $\frac{x}{e^x-1}=\sum_{n\ge 0}B_n\frac{x^n}{n!}$, and let $E_0,E_1,E_2,\dots$ denote the Euler numbers, defined by $\sec x=\sum_{n\ge 0}E_n\frac{x^n}{n!}$ (so $E_{2k+1}=0$). For an odd prime $p$, let $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol.

Prove or disprove the following three statements.

(i) For every odd prime $p$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{28k^2+18k+3}{(-64)^k}\binom{2k}{k}^4\binom{3k}{k}\equiv 3p^2-\tfrac{7}{2}\,p^5 B_{p-3}\pmod{p^6},$$
and
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{28k^2+18k+3}{(-64)^k}\binom{2k}{k}^4\binom{3k}{k}\equiv 3p^2+6\Big(\tfrac{-1}{p}\Big)p^4 E_{p-3}\pmod{p^5}.$$

(ii) For every integer $n>1$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(28k^2+18k+3)\binom{2k}{k}^4\binom{3k}{k}(-64)^{n-1-k}\equiv 0\pmod{(2n+1)\,n^2\binom{2n}{n}^2}.$$

(iii) The identity
$$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(28k^2-18k+3)(-64)^k}{k^5\binom{2k}{k}^4\binom{3k}{k}}=-14\,\zeta(3)$$
holds, where $\zeta(3)=\sum_{n\ge 1}n^{-3}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Apéry-like series identity in part (iii), $\sum_{k\ge 1}(28k^2-18k+3)(-64)^k/(k^5\binom{2k}{k}^4\binom{3k}{k})=-14\zeta(3)$, has been confirmed by K. C. Au (around 2022) as part of a broader proof of Sun's conjectured rational $\zeta(3)$-series. The supercongruences in parts (i) and (ii) involving Bernoulli/Euler numbers and the binomial divisibility do not appear to have been fully verified in the literature; no proof was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: New series involving binomial coefficients (II)
status_evidence.snippet: Series of Apéry-like type involving products of binomial coefficients, including Sun's conjectures, with proofs by K. C. Au.
status_evidence.claim: K. C. Au proved Sun's conjectured Apéry-like rational series for ζ(3) of this form.

status_evidence.title: Open Conjectures on Congruences (Sun)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture A40 lists supercongruences mod p^6 and mod p^5 with Bernoulli/Euler numbers, plus the closed-form ζ(3) series.
status_evidence.claim: The supercongruence parts (i) and (ii) are stated as open conjectures.
